Find Analyses

Source: R/analyses.R
og_analyses.Rd

Returns Analysis metadata, one row per identifier given, or the whole catalogue.

Usage

og_analyses(src, ids = NULL, releases = NULL)

Arguments

src

A Source, from og_api().

ids

Analysis identifiers, or NULL for the whole catalogue.

releases

Store Releases to use. NULL uses the one Store Release each GWAS Store serves, as does a GWAS Store id such as "OGS-00011". The API doesn't say which Store Release of a GWAS Store is latest, so if a GWAS Store serves several, opengwasr stops with opengwasr_release_selection_required and lists them: pin one as "<store_id>/<release_id>".

Value

A data frame: requested_id, id, then the API's metadata columns (store_id, analysis_id, analysis_label, assigned_ancestry, sample_size, release_id, ...).

Details

An Analysis is named <store_id>:<analysis_id>, such as OGS-00011:GCST90029007. A bare analysis_id, or an identifier from Legacy OpenGWAS, is accepted where it names exactly one Analysis. The requested_id column shows what you asked for and id the canonical id.

  • A legacy identifier whose analysis has a later release is answered by the successor, with a warning of class opengwasr_legacy_successor carrying requested_id and id.

  • An identifier that could name more than one Analysis raises opengwasr_ambiguous_analysis, with the candidates in candidates.

  • An identifier that names no Analysis, or one that has been retired, raises opengwasr_analysis_not_found (opengwasr_analysis_retired too when retired), the classes of the API's own codes. The condition carries the identifiers in ids, the API's reason for each where it gave one in api_reasons (NA otherwise), and, for a retired Analysis, every successor the API named in superseded_by.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
src <- og_api()
og_analyses(src, c("OGS-00011:GCST90029007", "ukb-b-19953"))
catalogue <- og_analyses(src)
} # }
